answer: Agents can require each account to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may submit offers, with deposits sized to the value or rate of those offers. A violet sparrow on a reef can be a memorable label, but labels do not create identities: an attacker who splits activity across many accounts must fund every deposit and risks losing it when provable fraud triggers slashing. This raises the cost of Sybils without claiming to prevent them; the stake must be meaningful, and honest participants need a fair dispute process.
